newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson lifts Swedish shares to record close.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson lifts Swedish shares to record close.

text.p: A surge in telecoms group Ericsson lifted Swedish shares to a record high close on Wednesday.
The exchange's general index jumped two percent to a new record level of 3,226.66, beating its July 30 record of 3,191.87, in fairly good turnover of 4.79 billion crowns.

"There has been large pressure on the sell side in Ericsson recently and now when U.S. buyers stepped in there was this reaction upwards," a trader said. Another dealer said investors were probably changing to Ericsson from Nokia.
"It feels as if Ericsson's report was stronger (than Nokia's)," he said.
Ericsson also benefited from the stronger dollar.

Appliance group Electrolux and engineer Atlas Copco attracted attention as they released better than expected six-month results. Electrolux ended four crowns lower at 611 while Atlas Copco jumped nine to 243.

The dollar also helped auto group Volvo that rose 6.5 crowns to 222 and the forestry sector which jumped 3.1 percent. Forestry was also supported by Stora's six-month report and rosier sector outlook a day earlier.

"The forestry sector should outperform the general index the rest of the year. Stora's report confirms that demand is strong and that the price trend is up on virtually all products," said Torbjorn Tufvesson, analyst at Carnegie.
